title: Rabbi Shimon ben Netanel
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was the fourth of the five great students of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, as in Avot 2:8, and his teacher said of him that he feared Heaven. When he said to them, “Go out and see which is the straight path a person should choose for himself,” Rabbi Shimon ben Netanel said: “One who sees what will come to be.” “Which is the evil path that a person should distance himself from?” He said: “One who borrows and does not repay,” etc. His precious saying remains to us there, 2:13: “Be careful with the reading of Shema and with prayer; and when you pray, do not make your prayer fixed, but [a plea for] mercy … and do not be wicked in your own eyes.”

In Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and his students were walking on the road, and Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh expounded the Work of the Chariot. When Rabbi Yosef HaKohen and Rabbi Shimon ben Netanel heard, they too opened with the Work of the Chariot … and a heavenly voice went out and said to them: “Behold, the place is free for you and the banquet hall is spread for you; you and your students are destined for the third group.” In Chagigah 14a the incident is cited, and there the reading is Rabbi Yehoshua, not Rabbi Shimon ben Netanel.

We find in Tosefta Avodah Zarah, chapter 3: an incident in which Rabban Gamliel the Elder married his daughter to Shimon ben Netanel the Kohen and stipulated with him that she would not prepare foods in purity on his account.

notes.text: Hyman writes fearing Heaven, so the draft’s fearing sin is restored to his wording; the former note wrongly claimed to render him as given. The stipulated purity work is on his account, not an established supervisory role; no new judgment about Shimon’s status is admitted. Saved Machon Mamre Tosefta Avodah Zarah3 has granddaughter, while Hyman says daughter; both are disclosed. מעשת is read as מעשה.

The consulted Avot 2:8 reads “fearing sin,” whereas Hyman writes “fearing Heaven”; the body preserves Hyman. Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1 directly names Yosef HaKohen and Shimon ben Netanel. Machon Mamre Tosefta Avodah Zarah 3:3 has Gamliel’s granddaughter, not Hyman’s daughter, and preserves the purity stipulation on his account; no new status judgment is admitted.
